synopsis: With M'uru hidden in Silvermoon, the kingdom's leaders and magisters turn from possession to use. Rommath argues that a broken people have the right to seize whatever power can keep them alive, while Astalor rejects mere draining and devises the colder method by which the captive naaru can be subjugated into a sustained, disciplined source of Light. Chosen because of her former bond to the Light and her capacity to bear what others would not, Liadrin becomes the first true vessel and central figure of this new order: she does not restore the old priesthood, but submits herself to a sacred wrong as the price of survival. Through private conversations and the example of her leadership, she teaches Falanaras to carry that burden without forgetting how they obtained it, while Theron is drawn to the order's promise of disciplined strength in service to Quel'Thalas. In a private exchange among the three friends, Falanaras and Theron state that they intend to become Blood Knights; Lethira answers, with characteristic sarcasm, that she will stick to her bow. When the Blood Knights are founded, Falanaras and Theron take the oath while Lethira continues in the ranger's path, and Falanaras emerges steadied rather than absolved, proud of the order he has chosen while fully aware that its foundation remains a wound.
title: Chapter 11: The First Blood Knights
